title: Stock Futures Rise as Wall Street Ends Volatile Holiday Week – Live CNBC Updates
body:
U.S. equity futures nudged higher on Thursday night, signaling a modest rebound as investors closed out a tumultuous week that was truncated by the Thanksgiving holiday. The S&P 500 futures were up about 0.7%, while Nasdaq‑100 contracts climbed roughly 0.8% and Dow Jones‑linked futures added 0.5%. The modest gains came after a series of volatile moves earlier in the week, including a sharp sell‑off on Wednesday that saw the S&P 500 plunge more than 2% before stabilizing late in the session.

The rally in futures reflects a mix of factors that have kept markets on edge. Inflation data released earlier in the week showed consumer prices rising at a slower pace than expected, easing some of the pressure on the Federal Reserve’s rate‑cut narrative. At the same time, corporate earnings reports have been a mixed bag, with technology giants delivering better‑than‑expected results, while several industrial and consumer‑discretionary firms warned of softer demand ahead of the holiday season. The combination of softer inflation and uneven earnings has left investors weighing the odds of a more accommodative monetary stance against the risk of a slowdown in consumer spending.

Geopolitical headlines also added to the market’s jittery mood. Ongoing tensions in the Middle East and renewed concerns about supply chain disruptions in Asia have kept risk‑averse investors cautious. Yet, the futures market’s upward tick suggests that traders are beginning to price in a “holiday‑season” rally, a pattern historically observed when the calendar year draws to a close and investors reposition portfolios ahead of year‑end tax considerations. Historically, the final week of November and early December have seen modest gains in the major indices, as fund managers lock in performance and rebalance holdings.

Analysts note that the modest rise in futures does not guarantee a smooth finish to the week. “We’re still seeing a lot of uncertainty surrounding the Fed’s next move, and the market is trying to digest a patchwork of earnings, inflation, and geopolitical data,” said Laura Chen, senior market strategist at Meridian Capital. “If the Fed signals a more aggressive stance on rates, or if any of the earnings disappoint, we could see the momentum reverse quickly.” Moreover, the shortened trading calendar means that any significant news could have an outsized impact on the limited number of sessions remaining before the market closes for the year‑end holidays.

Volume in the futures market has been relatively light compared with typical trading days, a common occurrence when a holiday looms. Thin trading can amplify price swings, making it harder for investors to gauge the true direction of the market. Nevertheless, the modest uptick in futures indicates that the prevailing sentiment is cautiously optimistic, with many market participants betting that the holiday lull will provide a brief respite from the recent turbulence.

Looking ahead, the next few trading sessions will be crucial in setting the tone for December and the final quarter of 2024. Investors will be watching closely for the Federal Reserve’s policy guidance, upcoming corporate earnings, and any fresh developments in global trade or geopolitical hotspots. If inflation continues to ease and earnings beat expectations, the market could sustain its modest gains and potentially finish the year on a positive note. Conversely, any resurgence of inflationary pressure or a hawkish Fed stance could reignite volatility, underscoring the delicate balance that will define the closing weeks of the trading year.
